facts.raw_span: A 55-year-old woman presented with generalized gum bleeding and halitosis
generalized bleeding on probing
clinical attachment loss
radiographs showed generalized alveolar bone loss consistent with stage II, grade II periodontitis
periapical radiographs of the maxillary central incisors revealed cervical areas of rarefaction
both central incisors were normal in color, responded normally to cold testing, and were asymptomatic to percussion and palpation
A 5 mm probing depth was recorded on the palatal aspects of both teeth

Cone-beam computed tomography demonstrated radiolucent resorptive lesions cervically on the palatal aspects of teeth #11 and #21, originating from the external palatal surface and perforating into the pulp space
asymptomatic irreversible pulpitis with normal apical tissues and external cervical resorption
her medical history was noncontributory
extraoral examination was unremarkable
she had undergone orthodontic treatment 18 years earlier
